chapters.title: Start
chapters.sourcePressure: Startup progress is redefined as learning how to build a sustainable business under extreme uncertainty, not as shipping features or looking busy.
chapters.coreMove: Replace output theater with a build-measure-learn loop that reduces one real uncertainty about customers or viability.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating lean startup as permission to move fast, be scrappy, or celebrate productivity without asking what was learned.

chapters.title: Define
chapters.sourcePressure: Entrepreneurship is defined by creating something new under uncertainty, whether the team is in a startup, corporation, nonprofit, government office, or school.
chapters.coreMove: Classify work by uncertainty rather than by the organization's costume, then choose a management system that fits that condition.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming startup means small company, founder identity, venture funding, or loosened discipline.

chapters.title: Learn
chapters.sourcePressure: Validated learning becomes the startup's true output, and learning only counts when empirical evidence proves something about the customer, product, or business model.
chapters.coreMove: Make every claimed lesson earn its status by tying it to evidence strong enough to change the next decision.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling any thoughtful reflection, positive comment, or team debrief learning.

chapters.title: Experiment
chapters.sourcePressure: Startup work is treated as hypothesis-driven experimentation, especially around value and growth, because live tests reveal more than market research under uncertainty.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a hopeful belief into a concrete experiment where customer behavior can answer value or growth directly.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating research, interviews, surveys, or opinions with experiments that test behavior.

chapters.title: Leap
chapters.sourcePressure: The riskiest leap-of-faith assumptions must be named and tested first because their failure can break the entire business.
chapters.coreMove: Rank assumptions by how much damage their failure would do, then test the most dangerous leap before polishing safer details.
chapters.commonMisread: Listing assumptions as paperwork while continuing to build around the frightening one.

chapters.title: Test
chapters.sourcePressure: The minimum viable product is a learning instrument that completes one build-measure-learn cycle with minimum waste, including low-fidelity, video, concierge, or manual tests.
chapters.coreMove: Build the smallest honest learning device that can expose the assumption, even if it looks less like a finished product.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating MVP as a cheap, sloppy version of the whole product or as a launch shortcut.

chapters.title: Measure
chapters.sourcePressure: Innovation accounting replaces vanity metrics with actionable, accessible, auditable evidence built from baselines, cohorts, and tuning the engine before pivot-or-persevere decisions.
chapters.coreMove: Convert impressive numbers into decision-ready measurements that show whether a specific engine is improving.
chapters.commonMisread: Using bigger dashboards, totals, or celebratory growth charts as proof of progress.

chapters.title: Pivot (or Persevere)
chapters.sourcePressure: A pivot is a structured course correction that tests a new core hypothesis, and the decision should come from validated learning rather than attachment.
chapters.coreMove: Use evidence to decide whether to persevere or make a specific course correction that preserves learning while changing the hypothesis.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling any change a pivot, or treating persistence as virtue after the evidence has stopped improving.

chapters.title: Batch
chapters.sourcePressure: Small batches shorten feedback distance, while large batches hide defects, create inventory-like waste, and delay correction; continuous deployment is one expression of this learning-speed logic.
chapters.coreMove: Shrink the unit of work until problems surface while they are still cheap enough to fix.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing batch size as a productivity hack instead of a way to expose reality earlier.

chapters.title: Grow
chapters.sourcePressure: Sustainable growth comes from identifying and tuning the right engine, sticky, viral, or paid, instead of hoping for generic user growth.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose the actual growth engine and tune the variable that makes that engine sustainable.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating growth as more marketing, more users, or any upward graph.

chapters.title: Adapt
chapters.sourcePressure: Adaptive organizations use feedback loops and Five Whys to improve quality and process without smothering learning speed, especially when recurring technical problems trace to human systems.
chapters.coreMove: Trace repeated failures past the visible incident into the human system that keeps producing them, then change the system without freezing the work.
chapters.commonMisread: Adding process after every mistake until the organization becomes slower but no wiser.

chapters.title: Innovate
chapters.sourcePressure: Established organizations need sandboxes, autonomy, protected resources, incentives, protection, and accountability so internal ventures can learn before the core business crushes them.
chapters.coreMove: Design a bounded innovation space where a new idea has enough autonomy to learn and enough accountability to stay honest.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming an innovation program needs only encouragement, budget, or executive slogans.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Waste Not
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing synthesis frames waste as wasted effort, wasted learning, and wasted opportunity caused by applying old management habits under uncertainty.
chapters.coreMove: Audit where effort is being spent before learning arrives, then pull the truth earlier so insight is not discarded or bought too late.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the epilogue to thrift, efficiency, or a recap of lean tools.

chapters.title: Join the Movement
chapters.sourcePressure: The final chapter widens lean startup from tactic to broader innovation practice and asks readers to apply and spread the discipline concretely.
chapters.coreMove: Turn agreement with the method into one adopted practice that changes how a real team makes uncertain decisions.
chapters.commonMisread: Ending with inspiration, movement rhetoric, or admiration without operational adoption.
